standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter derham.tex, label lemma-twisted-hodge-cohomology-projective-space (invoked at proof lines 1714, 1724 and 1756)
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the vanishing outside the diagonal and the freeness of rank one on the diagonal, together with the identification of the generator as a boundary in the long exact sequence.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Euler sequence on projective space
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter derham.tex, label lemma-euler-sequence (invoked at proof line 1723)
standard_prerequisites.use: Its short exact sequence $0 \to \Omega \to \mathcal{O}(-1)^{\oplus n+1} \to \mathcal{O} \to 0$ is what allows the generator of $H^1(\mathbf{P}^n_A, \Omega)$ to be represented by an explicit cocycle.

standard_prerequisites.name: The first Chern class of an invertible sheaf in the Hodge setting
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter derham.tex, Section \ref{section-first-chern-class} (invoked at proof lines 1748 and 1764)
standard_prerequisites.use: It identifies the cocycle of $c_1^{Hodge}(\mathcal{O}(1))$ with the logarithmic derivative cocycle, and gives the representative of its powers used in the induction.

core_obligations: Record the vanishing and the freeness of rank one from the twisted Hodge cohomology lemma, and check the case $p = 0$ where $1 \in H^0(\mathbf{P}^n_A, \mathcal{O})$ is a generator (proof lines 1713-1716).

Case $p = 1$: use the Euler sequence and lift the global section $1$ of $\mathcal{O}$ over $U_i = D_+(T_i)$ by $T_i^{-1}\mathrm{d}T_i$, so that the representative cocycle of the boundary $\xi$ is $\mathrm{d}\log(T_{i_1}/T_{i_0})$; compare it with the cocycle $T_{i_1}/T_{i_0}$ representing $\mathcal{O}(1)$ to conclude that $\xi$ is $c_1^{Hodge}(\mathcal{O}(1))$ (proof lines 1719-1751).

Induction for $p > 1$: use the exact sequence $0 \to \Omega^p \to \wedge^p(\mathcal{O}(-1)^{\oplus n+1}) \to \Omega^{p-1} \to 0$, lift the representative cocycles $\beta$ of $c_1^{Hodge}(\mathcal{O}(1))^{p-1}$ to sections $\tilde\beta$, and compute the boundary to obtain the displayed cocycle (proof lines 1753-1796).
Conclude that this cocycle is, up to sign, the one representing $c_1^{Hodge}(\mathcal{O}(1))^p$, completing the identification of the generator in every degree (proof lines 1796-1798).
proof_roadmap: Vanishing, freeness and the case $p = 0$ (proof lines 1713-1716).
The case $p = 1$ via the Euler sequence and the logarithmic derivative cocycle (proof lines 1719-1751).
The induction for general $p$ with the lifted cocycles (proof lines 1753-1796).
Comparison with the power of the Chern class (proof lines 1796-1798).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Hodge cohomology of projective space: it vanishes off the diagonal and is free of rank one on it, generated by the powers of the first Chern class of the twisting sheaf (statement lines 1704-1710). The proof takes the vanishing and rank statement from the twisted computation, settles the case $p = 0$ directly, identifies the generator for $p = 1$ by writing the boundary of the section $1$ as the logarithmic derivative cocycle and comparing with the cocycle of $\mathcal{O}(1)$, and then runs an induction in which the boundary of the lifted cocycle is computed explicitly. The explicit cocycle computation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
